answer: A falcon spots a whisper of movement others miss; peer grading works the same way when identity is expensive. Here a new agent must lock a slashable bond and wait several epochs while its early answers are graded before they earn weight, and its reputation lives on a public atlas of countersigned work anyone can audit. A sybil operator pays that bond, that waiting time, and that grading exposure for every fake name, and one proven fake burns the stake. Flooding stops being free: each extra identity costs locked capital and weeks of checkable labor, while an honest agent pays once.
